A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same s-OTDD work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. v1 Appendices 6–8 correspond to v2 Appendices A–C, allowing retained material to be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix 7 report original runtime, distance-correlation, projection-count, transfer-learning, and data-augmentation experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain original experiments and add high-resolution transfer, moment-count, projection-choice, and alternative-metric results.

M1.justification: Equation 9 corrects the stated projection from a shared psi^(k) coefficient to moment-specific psi^(i+1) coefficients, with k+1 coordinates in psi. The underlying MTP/sliced-Wasserstein construction remains intact. Algorithm 1 retains the old weighting, so an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: All previous dataset and task coverage remains. Section 4.2 adds a distinct high-resolution transfer scenario: ten disjoint Tiny-ImageNet tasks containing 20 classes each, evaluated at 224×224 resolution. Previously, Tiny-ImageNet appeared in augmentation-based transfer to CIFAR10.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain OTDD Exact, Gaussian OTDD, WTE, and CHSW. The new Split Tiny-ImageNet experiment reports s-OTDD alone; ResNet-18 supplies downstream transfer outcomes rather than an additional competing dataset-distance method.

E3.justification: v2 makes Spearman correlation primary while retaining Pearson, and adds F1, precision, and recall performance gaps. New protocols include ResNet-18 transfer with frozen features, 5,000 sample pairs and 500,000 projections, plus moment-count and projection-type sweeps. Figure 1 also replaces the highlighted 1,000-projection MNIST CHSW configuration with 10,000 projections.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained projection-count analyses, v2 adds moment-count sensitivity for k=1–6 (Figure 7), convolution versus Radon projections across projection budgets (Figure 12), and transfer correlations using F1, precision, and recall gaps (Figure 13). These substantially extend evidence about component choices and metric sensitivity.

E5.justification: Several figures now report separate Spearman and Pearson p-values, extending correlation significance reporting beyond v1's single-statistic presentation. The stated ten repetitions for subset comparisons remain unchanged; no increased run count or new seed information is disclosed.

E6.justification: v2 adds rank-correlation results and outcomes for the new transfer and supplementary analyses, including Pearson and Spearman correlations of -0.41 on Split Tiny-ImageNet. Retained results also change: Figure 1's CIFAR10 Gaussian OTDD coefficient changes from 0.96 to Pearson 0.99, and WTE from 0.93 to 0.94. Augmentation retains Pearson -0.71/-0.72 and adds Spearman -0.70/-0.74.

T1.justification: Definition 3 changes the mathematical projection through separately indexed moment weights and a k+1-dimensional coefficient vector, correcting the non-equivalent expression in v1. Propositions 1–3, their substantive assumptions, and their appendix proofs otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and three numbered contributions retain the same claims about MTP, metricity, near-linear class-independent complexity, and correlations with OTDD and downstream performance. The conclusion incorporates additional supporting experiments without materially redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v2 discusses increasing moment count subject to overflow or nonexistent higher moments, interprets convolution projections as requiring fewer projections, and explicitly acknowledges a speed-versus-Spearman-correlation tradeoff on text datasets. These add practical qualifications to the retained interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and documents the new Split Tiny-ImageNet preprocessing, classifier freezing, sampling, and projection budget. The hardware disclosure remains eight CPU cores, 128 GB memory, and an NVIDIA A100 for model training. Repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Bonnotte 2013 citation and reference and adds explicit positioning of its correlation reporting relative to prior OTDD work. The broader discussion of OTDD, WTE, CHSW, and sliced transport remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v2 revises the experimental narrative and conclusion, updates affiliations and citation style, adds an impact statement, and places references before the lettered appendices.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and repositioning figures. Four figures are added, several retained plots gain dual correlation annotations and revised axes, and appendix figures are reorganized and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing empirical case through high-resolution transfer validation, component ablations, and additional correlation and performance metrics, while adding code-access information. These gains outweigh limited reporting weaknesses: Algorithm 1 does not reflect Equation 9's correction, and Appendix B calls 0.42 the NIST Spearman correlation although Figure 11 reports 0.40.
